note: CME observed to the E only in STEREO A COR2, likely not seen in other coronagraphs due to the occulting disk and/or faint leading edge. The source may be an eruption from AR 14536 centered around N03W32, observed as slow dimming, brightening, and field line movement in SDO AIA 171/193 starting around 2026-09-23T21:06Z. In STEREO A COR2, there is a faint leading edge observed already far in the east field-of-view after a data gap ends at 2026-09-24T01:23Z that better corresponds to this eruption time, but is also plausible to be a candidate source for this CME.

note: Bright lightbulb-shaped CME seen to the SW in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1 and STEREO A COR2. Its source is a large prominence seen lifting from behind the SW limb starting at 2026-09-26T18:28Z (best seen in GOES SUVI 304), with source location seen on disk, close to the SW limb in STEREO A EUV 304/195 imagery. In EUV A 195 imagery we see an ejecta, as well as dimming and bright post-eruptive arcades. The erupting filament is also seen in AIA 171 and faintly in AIA 304, and ejecta and opening of field lines are seen off/close behind the SW limb in GOES SUVI 286. The erupting filament stretches very approximately from ~S25W15 (mostly dimming) to ~S20W80 (ejecta and post-eruptive arcades), as seen from STEREO A perspective, so the filament can be estimated as centered very approximately at ~S20W135 from the SDO perspective.
